text:
mika: Handoff: new cloud account + VPC for 'northstar' GPU region (eu-north-1). I set up the org/project skeleton and initial infra TF state. Posting quick runbook + open items.
jonas: Thanks — can you drop the workspace/terraform commands?
mika: Sure. main steps I ran: 
```bash
# create workspace and select region
terraform workspace new northstar || terraform workspace select northstar
terraform init
terraform apply -var 'region=eu-north-1' -auto-approve
```
mika: Outputs: shared-services-vpc id, ops-subnet ids, private-hosting subnet, transit-gw placeholder. Route tables and NACLs applied.
prasanna: Did you pick CIDR ranges? We need to avoid overlap with customer VPCs and our eu backbone.
mika: Yes — picked 10.64.0.0/16 for shared-services, 10.65.0.0/16 for compute (reserved for GPU clusters). I added comments in TF vars file: /infra/networking/northstar/vars.tf.
amy: Are ENI and ENI per-instance limits addressed? Dense GPU nodes will need plenty of IPs.
mika: Good catch. Using /22 per AZ for nodepools by default. Will request instance-level ENI quota bump for p4d/h100 families. I added a Jira card: INFRA-2243 (quota requests + spot vs on-demand planning).
leo: What about VPC peering / Transit Gateway? We need cluster-control-plane access to control plane in prod account.
mika: Configured TGW attachment from shared-services to prod-control plane account. Transit route propagation enabled. Put explicit deny rule for cross-account internet egress except via NAT in shared-services.
jonas: Any private endpoints for registry/s3?
mika: Yes — S3 VPC gateway endpoint and ECR interface endpoints in shared-services-vpc. Also Secrets Manager and KMS endpoints. KMS key created in the project with key policy granting service accounts from kube-control plane role. KMS key arn: arn:aws:kms:eu-north-1:111222333444:key/abcd-ef01
infra-bot: Reminder: aws default VPC limits: 5 per region. You created 1 custom VPC.
prasanna: Are we enabling flow logs and ENCRYPTION at rest?
mika: Flow logs enabled and sent to central logging account via CloudWatch logs subscription. S3 bucket has default encryption AES256, bucket policy to block public access.
amy: How should we validate connectivity to GPU nodes once cluster is up?
mika: Plan: (1) smoke VM in compute subnet with curl to registry.private.local, (2) run kubectl on bastion to spin demo pod with GPU resource request, (3) check nv_peer_mem and nvidia-smi in privileged debug pod. Added steps in checklist below.
jonas: Post the checklist please.
mika: Checklist (short):
- Verify IAM roles: cluster-node role, cluster-control role, kms-grant (commands in runbook)
- Confirm ENI + IP capacity per AZ (/22s allocated)
- Request GPU quota (P4d/H100) and validate via support ticket INFRA-2243
- TGW attachment & route propagation verified
- Private endpoints (S3/ECR/Secrets/KMS) reachable from compute subnet
- Flow logs visible in central logs (last 15m)
- Security groups: only control-plane CIDR + ops bastion allowed on 10250/22 and 22
- KMS key policy includes cross-account trust for prod-control-plane
- Terraform state locked in s3 backend (dynamodb locking)
- VPC Flow log sampling set to '10%' for now to limit costs
- Cost tags: environment:northstar, owner:infra, project:gpu-onboard
leo: Cost note — using /22 per AZ is a bit wasteful initially. Can we start /24 and expand via additional subnets later?
mika: We can but node auto-scaling with ENI shortages is risky. For initial launch, we reserve /22 per AZ to avoid hitting ENI bottlenecks. Will review after 2 weeks of usage.
prasanna: Also need to coordinate with cloud procurement for Dedicated capacity commitments — if sales plans to reserve racks, we might get quota bumps faster.
amy: Regarding cluster naming and resource tags — please include cluster=rs-northstar-prod and billing-owner tag.
mika: Done. TF module sets tags for all compute resources. See module: modules/aws-gpu-cluster/tags.tf
jonas: Any outstanding security review?
mika: Quick review with security done, final review scheduled tomorrow 10:00. Notes: enable EBS encryption, no public SGs, bastion with ephemeral keys.
leo: How do we run the validation commands once infra ready?
mika: Validation snippet: 
```bash
# smoke VM ssh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/northstar-bastion ubuntu@bastion.northstar.internal
# from bastion
curl -v http://ecr.private.local/v2/
# kube validation
kubectl --kubeconfig=/etc/kube/northstar get nodes -o wide
kubectl run gpu-test --image=nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:11.8-base --limits="nvidia.com/gpu=1" -- sleep 3600
kubectl logs -f $(kubectl get pods -l run=gpu-test -o name) -n default
```
mika: Open items: (A) quota ticket INFRA-2243 pending AWS reply; (B) AZ mapping confirmation from network team for eu-north-1 (I used azs: eu-north-1a,b,c but AWS sometimes has different names) ; (C) Confirm Terraform backend permissions for ops SRE service account.
amy: I'll own A (quota ticket).
prasanna: I'll validate AZ mapping and ENI counts.
leo: I'll do the smoke validation once nodes provisioned.
jonas: If everything looks good post-validation, what's handoff?
mika: Handoff steps to product: (1) update Runbook in docs repo with final TF outputs & kubeconfig location, (2) mark account as 'live' in inventory, (3) open post-onboard cost watch dashboard for first 72h, (4) schedule 1-week cadence for tuning.
jonas: Ack.
infra-bot: Scheduled reminder created: post-onboard cost check in 72h. (reminder id: r-99233) :white_check_mark:
mika: Thanks everyone. If no objections I'll promote the TF state to 'live' in 30m. Please reply with :thumbsup: or flag issues.
